neighbours.label: the first digit of an angle written in degrees (180°, 270°, 360-degree), where the number is a rotation, heading or angle; the same numbers as counts, prices or oven temperatures stay quiet
fire: Turn the valve handle 180° until the arrow points down.
The turret can swing through a full 360° in under ten seconds.
After take-off the pilot turned to a heading of 270° and climbed.
The stage lights sweep in a 360-degree circle above the crowd.
Flip the photo, then rotate it 270° so the text reads correctly.
The crane arm pivots 180° to reach the far side of the dock.
The compass showed a bearing of 135° as we left the harbour.
Twist the lid 45° clockwise and lift it off the jar.
quiet: Turn the valve handle twice until the arrow points down.
The turret can fire 360 rounds in under ten seconds.
After take-off the pilot climbed to 270 metres and levelled off.
The stage lights cost 360 dollars each and hang above the crowd.
Flip the photo, then shrink it to 270 pixels so the text fits.
The crane arm lifts 180 tonnes to the far side of the dock.
The harbour had 135 boats moored as we left in the morning.
Twist the lid for 45 seconds and lift it off the jar.

notes: Card: peaks on '3', '4', '2', '1' in '360°', '45 deg', '270°', '45-degree angle'; the - pole fires just before an angle is stated ('rotation angle in degrees'). Probes: '270° … 180°' 0.60, '360-degree view' 0.45, '180°' 0.42, '45-degree angle' 0.34, '30, 60 and 90 degrees' 0.29, '30° angle' 0.17, '90 degrees' (knees) 0.04, '350 degrees' (oven) 0.10, 360 houses 0.02.
